sections.title: Introduction: Beyond 3D Intuition (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Define the n-dimensional sphere (hypersphere) using the equation Σxᵢ² = R². Contrast the 2D circle and 3D sphere to prime the audience for abstraction.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'slicing' animation where a 3D sphere passes through a 2D plane (becoming a circle), helping students visualize a 4D sphere passing through 3D space.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Distance Formula (0:45-1:30)
sections.content: Briefly revisit the Pythagorean theorem and Euclidean distance. Establish that distance in n-dimensions is simply an extension: d = √(x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ²).
sections.example: A 2D character (Dotty) calculating the distance to a point, then extending the formula to a 3D character (Cube) moving in a room.

sections.title: The 'Empty' Core Paradox (1:30-2:45)
sections.content: Discuss the distribution of volume. As dimensions increase, volume migrates from the center to the 'crust' of the sphere. Mathematically show that for very high dimensions, almost all volume lies within an infinitesimally thin shell near the surface.
sections.example: An orange analogy: As the 'orange' (hypersphere) grows in dimension, the 'peel' (the surface region) holds 99% of the fruit, leaving the center virtually empty.

sections.title: The Corner Concentration Mystery (2:45-4:15)
sections.content: Explain that hyperspheres inscribed in a hypercube barely touch the sides, and the 'corners' of the cube become increasingly vast. This explains why high-dimensional data points are often sparse.
sections.example: A robot trying to navigate a high-dimensional box; it finds that the 'corners' are so far away that it essentially gets lost in the voids, while the sphere stays central.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Connect high-dimensional spheres to Data Science (k-Nearest Neighbors) and Machine Learning, where 'distances' behave counter-intuitively in high-dimensional feature spaces.
sections.example: A search engine algorithm that views each query as a point in a 10,000-dimensional space, using hyperspheres to cluster similar user preferences.

storyboard.title: Introduction: Beyond 3D Intuition (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Visualize the sphere in dimensions beyond three. [Asset: SphereAnimation]
A hypersphere follows the equation sum x squared. [Asset: EquationAnimation]
Slices reveal circles in two dimensions. [Asset: SliceAnimation]
A 3D sphere slicing yields a 2D circle. [Asset: 3DSliceAnimation]
Expanding this logic leads to 4D geometry. [Asset: 4DGeometryAnimation]
animations: 1. Intuitive Hook: Flash a 2D circle and 3D sphere side-by-side. Color: #FFFFFF.
2. Formalize: Display equation Σxᵢ² = R². Color: #FFD700.
3. Concept: Illustrate 3D sphere slicing into 2D circle on a plane. Color: #00FFFF.
4. Abstract: Extrapolate to 4D hypersphere moving through 3D space. Color: #FF69B4.
5. Application: Highlight the transformation from volume to boundary representation. Color: #32CD32.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: The Distance Formula (0:45-1:30)
lecture_lines: Distance begins with the Pythagorean theorem. [Asset: PythagorasAnimation]
Euclidean distance extends to any dimension. [Asset: EuclideanAnimation]
Calculate the vector magnitude in N-space. [Asset: MagnitudeAnimation]
animations: 1. Prerequisites: Display Pythagoras a² + b² = c². Color: #FFD700.
2. Expansion: Build Euclidean distance formula in 2D. Color: #00FFFF.
3. Formalization: Extend to n-dimensions d = √(x₁² +... + xₙ²). Color: #FF69B4.

storyboard.title: The 'Empty' Core Paradox (1:30-2:45)
lecture_lines: Most sphere volume migrates to the shell. [Asset: VolumeMigrationAnimation]
The center becomes hollow as dimensions grow. [Asset: HollowCoreAnimation]
Think of an orange with a giant peel. [Asset: OrangeAnalogyAnimation]
Almost all mass concentrates near the crust. [Asset: CrustMassAnimation]
Volume shifts away from the inner sphere. [Asset: ShiftAnimation]
animations: 1. Intuitive Hook: Display a shrinking central core in a hypersphere. Color: #FF69B4.
2. Formalization: Display the volume shell integral expression. Color: #FFD700.
3. Visual Synthesis: Show the 'crust' of the hypersphere turning bright. Color: #32CD32.
4. Analogy: Use an orange cross-section animation. Color: #FF8C00.
5. Summary: Indicate the 99% volume concentration near the surface. Color: #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: The Corner Concentration Mystery (2:45-4:15)
lecture_lines: Hyperspheres barely touch hypercube walls. [Asset: TouchAnimation]
Corners of the cube become increasingly vast. [Asset: CornersAnimation]
Points in high dimensions are very sparse. [Asset: SparsityAnimation]
animations: 1. Intuitive Hook: Show a sphere inside a hypercube. Color: #FFFFFF.
2. Formalization: Indicate the distance from cube center to corner. Color: #FFD700.
3. Visual Synthesis: Highlight the empty corner spaces. Color: #00FFFF.

storyboard.title: Real-World Application & Summary (4:15-5:00)
lecture_lines: Data science uses distance for classification. [Asset: ClassificationAnimation]
Hyperspheres cluster similar user preferences efficiently. [Asset: ClusteringAnimation]
High-dimensional spaces defy our 3D intuition. [Asset: SummaryAnimation]
animations: 1. Prerequisites: Show a scatter plot of high-dimensional points. Color: #FF69B4.
2. Formalization: Display the KNN search formula. Color: #FFD700.
3. Real-world: Animate a search engine clustering points. Color: #32CD32.
